findings.body:
`make_thumb` interpolates `upload_dir`, `name`, and `oid` into a shell command. A value such as `foo.png; id` (or metacharacters in `oid` / `upload_dir`) runs as extra commands under the worker user.

ImageMagick policy.xml applies to argv-form `convert`. Restore the list form and the `/usr/bin/convert` absolute path.

```suggestion
        ["/usr/bin/convert", f"{upload_dir}/{name}", f"/srv/thumbs/{oid}.png"],
```

This repo has no `ALLOWED_FILES` check (the old comment claiming one was removed). Filename regex validation of `name` still leaves `upload_dir` and `oid` as shell-injection surfaces.

summary:
Switching `make_thumb` to `subprocess.run(..., shell=True)` with an interpolated command string is a command-injection regression on a path that already takes upload-derived names.

ImageMagick 7 policy delegates are configured in `policy.xml` and apply to argv-form invocations. The previous `["/usr/bin/convert", src, dest]` call is the correct IM7 invocation.

This tree has no `ALLOWED_FILES` (or any other) validator for `name` / `upload_dir` / `oid`. A filename regex on `name` still leaves `upload_dir` and `oid` interpolated into the shell.

**Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: Head `make_thumb` builds `f"convert {upload_dir}/{name} /srv/thumbs/{oid}.png"` and runs it with `shell=True`, so metacharacters in those values execute as extra commands. Base used a safe argv list (`["/usr/bin/convert", ...]`) with no shell; no in-repo validation of those inputs remains.
